correctness.rationale: For each of four invariant edge orbits of the exact 12-vertex graph, all Rips faces are reconstructed from independently recomputed shortest-path distances. Complete free-face collapse certificates produce two-complexes whose specified spanning trees and ordered one-live-edge triangle relators kill every fundamental group generator, with a unit-triangular integral boundary minor and free H2 ranks 2,1,4,4. Further exact collapse certificates give contractibility from radius three; scale one graphs and all diameters checked. Mod-two boundary ranks agree but are not the argument for integral homotopy.

evidence: Adamaszek 2011 Proposition 2.2 requires girth at least 3r+1, hence at r=2 girth at least 7. The Tietze graph has girth 3 and even faults outside the triangle preserve a triangle; deleting a triangle edge leaves girth 5, still below seven.

The 2017 metric-gluing paper treats metric gluing under geometric distance conditions and does not calculate this Tietze fault family. The 2021 paper provides general simplicial decompositions but no explicit edge-fault theorem.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The strongest candidate general stability theorem is explicitly inapplicable; the other full-text general methods do not supply numerical edge-orbit classification or its integral homotopy proofs. No stronger statement found that subsumes all four cases.

value.rationale: Exact natural complete classification of all eighteen single-link faults of the canonical Tietze graph, intrinsically grouped by the four unique-triangle distance orbits. Faults at the triangle yield sharper losses of integral sphere classes than other faults, while every graph becomes contractible at scale three; the result is a reproducible benchmark for persistent homotopy sensitivity, not just an arbitrary finite slice or a restatement of known intact-graph data.
